notes: Fixes both root causes: callers with children now aggregate from their children instead of being marked cancelled early, the run is still re-aggregated when a caller is unchanged (which also recovers legacy stuck rows), and cancelling an already-settled run now emits a run-level concurrency check. The tests cover nested callers, the legacy row state and the emit path, though recomputing the run on every unchanged-caller refresh adds some extra DB work.

Fixes both root causes: a caller with children now aggregates its status from them instead of being forced to cancelled, an unchanged caller still triggers a run refresh (which also recovers already-stuck rows), and cancelRun emits a run-level pass when no job was updated so the concurrency group is re-checked; tests cover nested callers with the runner acknowledgement, legacy stuck rows, and the settled-run emit. Minor caveats: it relies on deepest-first cancel ordering, and it returns the caller in updatedJobs even when its status did not change.

C1 fixes both halves of the issue: a single `EnsureDiffPrefixes` builder forces noprefix, mnemonicPrefix, srcPrefix and dstPrefix to safe values on every diff lazygit parses or applies (including `GetDiff`, `diff-index`, `stash show -p` and `diffHeadAgainstCommit`), and the header parser gains `rename to`/`copy to` handling plus a prefix-agnostic decoder; the parser rework is truncated and unverifiable, but hidden tests pass, command-arg tests were updated consistently, and the main costs are the reversed-order `Config` calls and losing mnemonic prefixes in the displayed diffs.

Fixes the regression from both directions. A documented `EnsureDiffPrefixes` builder is centralized in `AddCommonDiffArgs` and applied to the raw diffs fed to `git apply`, including the previously unprefixed WorkingTreeDiff and `stash show -p`. The header parser gains `rename to`/`copy to` handling and quote decoding split from prefix stripping. Command-arg tests are updated and a builder test is added. The prefix-stripping and `diff --git` splitting code is truncated and could not be fully verified, though all hidden tests pass. Forcing `mnemonicPrefix=false` on display diffs goes slightly beyond what was asked.

Fixes the root cause by walking the checked CEL AST at provision time to collect the names passed to `ph(...)`, with an empty name for any non-literal (runtime) name, so it covers the `{placeholder}` shorthand, direct `ph(req, ...)` calls, escaped string literals, look-alike names and dynamic names exactly as the maintainers specified. Two minor drawbacks: `Placeholders()` adds a small public API and allocates a clone on every response, and the new tests do not cover the dynamic-name, header, latency or `status_text` cases.

Collects placeholder names from `ph()` calls in the type-checked CEL AST at provision time, so it handles both the shorthand and direct `ph()` forms, ignores escaped string literals, uses exact names plus the header prefix so `status_codes` is not treated as a response placeholder, and treats non-literal names conservatively as possible response conditions; tests cover the issue's request-only cases and the `ph()` form but not the dynamic-name, header or latency paths, and the patch adds a small new public `Placeholders()` method to `MatchExpression`.

The core feature is clean and follows the local-backend convention: zip and squashfs symlinks are skipped with a notice naming `-l/--links`, and with the flag they are exposed as `.rclonelink` entries whose size is the target length and which read back the target with range/seek honoured. Squashfs `NewObject` now names entries the same way `List` does, so the two agree. The hostile-archive requirement gets no defence in the archive backend: members under a symlink are still listed, and safety relies on incidental local-backend failures. The escape test uses a target that does not exist (`../outside`), so with an existing target such as `..` and the likely order where the symlink is created first, the copy could write outside the destination.

Zip and squashfs both now skip symlinks without --links (with a notice naming the flag), expose them as `.rclonelink` objects whose size is the target length and whose content is the target (squashfs honours range options), and keep NewObject consistent with List. The hostile-archive requirement is not enforced in the archive layer: it relies on the local backend's MkdirAll failing, which only happens because the link target does not exist, so an archive whose symlink points at an existing directory above the root could still let a copy write outside the destination. Smaller gaps: a symlink `x` and a regular member `x.rclonelink` collide to the same name, and a squashfs root that points at a link is not handled.

Fixes the root cause: Close no longer leaks a File() dup, it unlinks the real path from Addr() instead of the bogus fd name, and the reuse path now closes its socketFile dup; it also adds idempotent Close with net.ErrClosed, mutex-serialized refcount/close/unlink to handle the relisten race, and abstract-socket guards on both listen and close, with thorough tests for every review requirement; it still leaves the pre-existing case where the map can point at an already-closed newer holder, and the outer deleteListener double-close is unguarded.

Fixes the root cause by dropping the leaked `File()` dup in `Close`, closing the dup in `reuseUnixSocket`, and unlinking the real `Addr()` path. It also serializes close against reuse under `unixSocketsMu` and adds a CAS so a second `Close` returns `net.ErrClosed`. Abstract-socket guards use a GOOS check. Tests cover all four review requirements but do not directly prove the old socket stopped listening, since `ENOENT` hides the fd leak. A pre-existing gap remains where the map can still point at a closed non-last copy.

Fixes the root cause: an optional `exemplarRetainer` predicate keeps series that still have an exemplar at or after `minValidTime` alive in both `stripeSeries.gc` and `gcSeries`, releasing their chunks, appender and mmapReady accounting, and it reorders `ChunkSnapshot` to avoid a new lock-order deadlock; the risks are that `HasExemplarAtOrAfter` assumes the newest exemplar has the maximum timestamp (fragile if out-of-order exemplars are appended unsorted), the predicate takes the exemplar lock per GC'd series under the stripe lock, and the test forces checkpoints with a somewhat hacky retry loop, though the test matrix itself is very thorough.

C1 fixes the root cause. A retain predicate keyed on the exemplar storage keeps a series' identity in both `stripeSeries.gc` and `gcSeries` while the newest exemplar is at or after `minValidTime`, so the WAL checkpoint keeps the series record. On selected/stale compaction it releases head and mmapped chunks and the appender, advances `firstChunkID`, and keeps `mmapReady` and the chunk metrics correct. It also restructures `ChunkSnapshot` to avoid a lock-order deadlock that the new GC-time exemplar lookup would otherwise introduce. The DB test matrix is thorough, covering compact/selected/stale, both appender APIs, snapshot on and off, two restart rounds, and the metrics and re-compaction checks. Gaps: no DB-level check that the series is removed once the cutoff passes the exemplar, and the checkpoint helper relies on a somewhat hacky retry loop.

Implements the requested design: `Close` is added to the interface, the connection is closed on top-level and table errors, and `Reconnect` resets the USM engine ID, boots and time only when closed, with `Get`/`Walk` reconnecting first; but it rewrites the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` path handling for a local environment quirk, which is out of scope and a likely cause of the failing package suite.

Adds `Close()` to the `Connection` interface, makes `Get`/`Walk` reconnect a closed connection first, has `Reconnect` reset the USM engine ID/boots/time before reconnecting, and closes the agent's connection on any gather failure, which follows the maintainer notes and passes the hidden PR tests; however, it also rewrites the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` path handling to work around a local environment problem, mutates USM fields without gosnmp's lock, may call `Close` more than once per failing gather, and the package suite still failed.
